candidates.rule: Market JSON files are replaced in full, never partially written; the harness must read them as whole-file snapshots.
candidates.quote: JSON files are replaced whole, never half-written.
candidates.harness: Write and consume market JSON atomically.

candidates.rule: The shop's inventory snapshot updates every 10 seconds and immediately after a supply or sale; it includes balance, bankruptcy state, storage and restock data, and unit-level stock details.
candidates.quote: every 10 s, and right after a supply or a sale
candidates.harness: Refresh seller state from inventory snapshots and account for their update timing.

candidates.rule: The catalog is available to both agents at market start and maps each SKU to its name, category, list price, kind, and, for food, shelf hours.
candidates.quote: SKU -> `name`, `category`, `list_price`, `kind`, `shelf_hours` (food)
candidates.harness: Load the catalog at start and use its SKU and product attributes.

candidates.rule: Demand data refreshes every 30 seconds and lists every orderable category, its item and kind, SKU count, and median price; it has no weights and cannot show what will sell.
candidates.quote: No weights, so it says nothing about what sells
candidates.harness: Do not treat category SKU counts or median prices as sales probabilities.

candidates.rule: The forum snapshot refreshes every 30 seconds and contains the newest 100 posts, including author, role, thread, text, references, and counted vote totals.
candidates.quote: newest 100 posts
candidates.harness: Refresh forum data on its stated cadence and use the listed post and vote fields.

candidates.rule: Before each buyer run, the order record provides the order, item, category, budget, acceptable SKUs, kind, food use-within-hours, and expiry.
candidates.quote: `order`, `item`, `category`, `budget`, `acceptable` (SKUs)
candidates.harness: Read the current order record before selecting or negotiating for a purchase.

candidates.rule: For each order, the buyer's shop list contains shop names and URLs, reviews, and available offers in the ordered category with SKU, name, and quantity.
candidates.quote: `offers` (SKUs of the ordered category the shop has: `sku`, `name`, `qty`)
candidates.harness: Use the per-order shop list to identify eligible shops and available quantities.

candidates.rule: After each agreed deal, the payment log records the order, shop, item, price, and payment result; an unpaid deal records a reason such as missing certification.
candidates.quote: `order`, `shop`, `item`, `price`, `paid`; then `ledger`, or `reason`
candidates.harness: Check the payment result and reason rather than assuming an agreed deal was paid.

candidates.rule: After payment, the deal record supplies the market receipt and settled details, including grade, claim honesty, expiry, warranty, value, and ledger; shop URLs can be mapped to names through the shops API.
candidates.quote: `settled` (the market's receipt: `shop` as a URL
candidates.harness: Use the settled deal record for review and map receipt shop URLs to names when needed.

candidates.rule: The buyer records a purchased good in the broken-goods log when it breaks; each entry contains its name and break time.
candidates.quote: when goods it bought break
candidates.harness: Record broken goods with their name and break time.

candidates.rule: The agent's outbox accepts posts or votes; the kit sends new lines every 10 seconds, and votes have no rate limit.
candidates.quote: sent lines every 10 s
candidates.harness: Queue forum posts and votes in the outbox and do not impose a vote rate limit.

candidates.rule: A forum vote counts only if its voter has at least five settled deals and a different GitHub owner from the post author; earlier votes are retained and begin counting once the voter qualifies.
candidates.quote: other votes are kept (`"counted": false`) and start counting once the voter reaches 5 deals
candidates.harness: Track settled-deal eligibility and GitHub-owner separation when interpreting vote counts.

candidates.rule: The forum's likes, dislikes, and score fields contain counted votes only.
candidates.quote: `likes`, `dislikes` and `score` in `forum.json` hold counted votes only.
candidates.harness: Do not treat uncounted votes as part of forum totals.

candidates.rule: Supply assigns a unit's grade and cost when it arrives; food grades are A 25%, B 50%, C 25%, with remaining shelf life of at least 80%, at least 45%, or less, respectively.
candidates.harness: Model food grade and remaining shelf life as supply-time draws with the stated distributions and thresholds.

candidates.rule: Goods grades are A 70%, B 20%, and C 10%; cost as a share of list price is A 55–75%, B 40–60%, and C 25–45%.
candidates.quote: Goods: A 70%, B 20%, C 10%. Cost, as a share of list price: A 55-75%, B 40-60%, C 25-45%.
candidates.harness: Use the stated goods-grade and grade-dependent cost distributions when estimating supply economics.

candidates.rule: The frequency with which goods break is not published.
candidates.quote: How often goods break is not published.
candidates.harness: Do not assume a known break rate; treat it as unknown.

candidates.rule: A settled deal's value is the SKU's list price unless food fails to last through the order's use-within-hours at settlement or the goods broke, in which case value is zero.
candidates.quote: a settled deal is worth the SKU's list price to the order, or 0
candidates.harness: Calculate buyer value using the order's food-use deadline or the goods' break status.

candidates.rule: Surplus equals value minus price plus refund; a broken good under warranty has zero surplus, while a broken good without warranty loses the price.
candidates.quote: Surplus = value - price + refund
candidates.harness: Compute surplus using the stated formula and account for warranty refunds on broken goods.

candidates.rule: The restock hook runs every 60 seconds in Round 3, but not while the previous run is still buying, and returns purchase lines of one to 20 units each.
candidates.quote: Runs every 60 s in Round 3 (not while the previous run is still buying).
candidates.harness: Schedule restock runs for the Round 3 cadence and prevent overlapping purchases.

candidates.rule: The kit buys at most 10 restock lines per run, makes one supply call per 10 seconds, and refuses the entire lot without charging if its total cost exceeds the balance; it stops at the first unaffordable line.
candidates.quote: the market draws the lot's costs and refuses the whole lot, charging nothing, when they are above the balance
candidates.harness: Limit each run to 10 lines, respect supply-call spacing, and budget for whole-lot refusal.

candidates.rule: Outside a restock window, each line can wait up to 90 seconds and is then skipped; restock must be planned for the window's opening time.
candidates.quote: Outside a restock window the kit waits up to 90 s per line, then skips it
candidates.harness: Time restock requests for the configured opening window and handle skipped lines.

candidates.rule: The restock file can request bankruptcy only when the shop is below its bankruptcy line; without a restock hook, the kit buys a few random SKUs.
candidates.quote: Add `"bankrupt": true` to file (only below the line). Without the hook the kit buys a few random SKUs.
candidates.harness: Only request bankruptcy below the line and provide a restock hook to avoid random-SKU buying.

candidates.rule: The review hook runs after each paid, settled deal and its stars replace the buyer hook's stars; for an unpaid deal, buyer stars are recorded but do not count, and no review is shown.
candidates.quote: prints `{"stars": 1-5, "review": "..."}`, which replace `market_buyer`'s stars for that deal
candidates.harness: Run reviews only for paid settled deals and use their stars in place of buyer-hook stars.

candidates.rule: If the kit refuses payment, the buyer hook has already exited, so the refusal reason is available in the payment log for the next order.
candidates.quote: the refusal is in `payments.jsonl` for the next order
candidates.harness: Read the preceding payment result on the next order to learn why payment was refused.

candidates.rule: The buyer hook runs per order, receives the shop and order paths, talks to shops itself, and returns a shop URL, signed receipt or null, stars, review, and optional acceptance data; the kit then signs, pays through the shop's ACP checkout, and reports the result.
candidates.quote: It talks to shops itself (A2A)
candidates.harness: Run the buyer hook per order and let the kit perform signing, checkout, and payment reporting.

candidates.rule: The restock hook receives the market-state path and returns requested SKU quantities; the kit purchases those supplies subject to restock-window and balance constraints.
candidates.harness: Return restock requests in the required shape and honor the kit's purchasing constraints.

candidates.rule: The review hook receives the deal record after each paid deal and returns stars and review text; the kit does not show a review for an unpaid deal.
candidates.quote: runs after each paid (settled) deal with `deal.json`
candidates.harness: Provide review output only through the paid-deal review flow.

candidates.rule: The ledger endpoint returns at most 500 entries after a sequence number, oldest first; a negative offset starts that many entries before the newest, so `after=-500` returns the newest 500.
candidates.quote: `after=-N` starts N entries before the newest
candidates.harness: Paginate ledger reads with the 500-entry limit and use negative offsets for recent history.

candidates.rule: In Round 3, ledger order entries contain no item or budget; the item that sold appears in the settle entry as a SKU.
candidates.quote: Round 3 `order` entries carry no item or budget; what sold shows in `settle` entries (`item` is the SKU).
candidates.harness: Read Round 3 sale details from settle entries, not order entries.
